terms.gloss: look at closely; think over, consider
evidence: Cic. Att. 7.13.3: sed velim cōnsīderēs, quid faciendum putēs
terms.comment: With an object, dē and the ablative, or an indirect question (Lewis & Short). First of looking carefully, as at the stars (lūcentia sīdera cōnsīderābāmus, Gell. 2.21.2), then of thinking a thing over.

evidence: Ter. Ph. 457: ego amplius dēlīberandum cēnseō
terms.comment: With dē, with utrum … an, or alone (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Sen. NQ 6.25: dē exitū cōgitāre (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: take into account, have regard for

phrases.latin: sed velim cōnsīderēs, quid faciendum putēs
phrases.english: but I’d like you to consider what you think should be done

phrases.latin: ego amplius dēlīberandum cēnseō: rēs magna est
phrases.english: I think we must weigh it up further: it’s a big matter

phrases.latin: Cōnsīderāte līlia agrī quōmodo crēscunt: nōn labōrant, neque nent.
phrases.english: Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin.
phrases.source: Vulg. Mt. 6.28 (the Stuttgart text has nec nent)

phrases.latin: Theodōrus saxa diū spectābat, dē gigante cōgitāns quī nōn est
phrases.english: Theo looked at the rocks for a long time, thinking about the giant who isn’t there
phrases.source: Libellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus
